title: Learning from Convenience Samples: A Case Study on Fine-Tuning LLMs for Survey Non-response in the German Longitudinal Election Study

bias_targets.methodology: Simulating systematic missing data by restricting fine-tuning datasets to biased convenience samples (e.g., only students, only unemployed individuals, or only residents of the Thuringia region) and evaluating how well the models can recover the true population-level vote share distributions using Macro F1 and Total Variation Distance.

Evaluating the predicted aggregate vote shares of LLMs against actual election ground truth to detect ideological skews, specifically identifying tendencies in zero-shot models to heavily over-predict left-leaning parties, over-predict extreme parties, and under-predict non-voters.
